newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes ample despite tight arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes ample despite tight arbitrage.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes were seen amply supplied into the U.S. Gulf despite a tighter Atlantic import arbitrage, with weaker Dated Brent likely to soon pry the window open again, traders said on Tuesday.
Imports were at steadily high levels, feeding refineries running at buoyant levels due to low product stocks.
"There has been real steady demand for regional crudes, and differentials are strong," a Gulf Coast refiner said, noting firm trades for Colombian crudes.
Vasconia was reported traded at West Texas Intermediate minus $1.95 fob for Oct, slightly firmer than recent trades.
Cano Limon was rumored done on Tuesday at WTI minus $1.55 fob, after being offered at minus $1.60 for Oct.
Traders cited strong demand for regional light, sweets such as Cusiana, pegged around Nov WTI minus 5-10 cents fob.
"There has been steady demand for Cusiana against Bonny Light and Brent barrels," a broker noted, despite their higher premium.
Ecuadorian Oriente for Oct delivery to the U.S. was at minus $1.80-85 a barrel, up from $2.00-$2.10 two months ago.
North Sea barrels were not spotted on their way to the U.S. due to the narrower import window, although falling Dated Brent prices suggested buying interest would surface again.
Oseberg for early Oct was seen still available to the U.S. and valued around WTI minus 10 cents cif.
In the aftermarket, Brent intermonth Oct/Nov traded twice at plus 65 cents, higher than earlier in the day.
An Oct Brent outright for a partial lot was heard done at $22.87 in late U.S. trade.
